title: Strong saturation of enhanced arrows
statement: Fix a small universe $\mathcal U$ and a containing ambient universe. Let $\mathscr C$ be a quasicategory, with equivalence edges, coherent functor categories and colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and smallness as in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Write $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathscr C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathscr C)$. A class $W$ of edges is strongly saturated if it contains equivalences, satisfies two-out-of-three on every compositional triangle, is closed under retracts of objects of $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathscr C)$, under homotopy pushouts (using the coherent pushout convention of [lem-coef-sheaf-flat-model]), and under all $\mathcal U$-small colimits of diagrams of objects of $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathscr C)$. A retract $a$ of $b$ is witnessed by arrows $a\to b\to a$ and a triangle identifying their composite with $\operatorname{id}_a$ in the coherent arrow category. Given any collection $S$ of edges, its strong saturation $\langle S\rangle$ is the intersection of all such classes containing $S$. Arrow colimits are computed on source and target.
